slides.texte_overlay:
hobbies that will make you
disgustingly intelligent

estimation games

guess numbers before you look them up: how tall that building is, how many people live in that city. checking your guesses builds a kind of intuition most people never train.

ask an expert

once a week, message someone who knows more than you about something and ask one specific question. most experts love being asked, and one answer can save you a month of googling.

drawing what you read

after reading something, close it and draw it from memory as a simple diagram. if you can't draw it, you didn't really understand it, you only recognised it.

brain breakfast

before your first scroll of the day, learn one thing in 5 minutes: how memory works, why rome fell, what a painting really means. feed your brain before the feed gets to it.

slides.texte_overlay:
songs in other languages

learn the lyrics of one song in a language you don't speak and look up what every line means. your brain gets new sounds, new grammar and a new way to see the world.
